case.question: I fish from the pier for salmon. For this week, how good do you expect pier fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven's pier.** I'd rate it 1 (below average). It's the only one of the three piers with a recent report naming a working lure: alewives or orange spoons.
- **Fish alewives or orange spoons first**, not spawn. Spawn was the only pier bait reported working at St. Joseph and South Haven.
- **Rate the other piers 1 too, but don't count on them.** St. Joseph and South Haven are both about 1 and reported slow.
- **Muskegon: no rating.** Its latest reports cover boats only, so I have no pier data for it.
- **For better odds, try a boat.** Boats were doing well at Muskegon and St. Joseph, but that's boat fishing, not pier.

## Why

- Grand Haven's pier is the only one of the three with a named working lure, alewives or orange spoons (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18).
- St. Joseph and South Haven pier anglers were catching only an occasional coho, on spawn (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18; South Haven, 2022-05-18).
- Muskegon has no pier report in the last eight weeks, so I can't rate its pier.
- I'd expect the piers to stay slow until the water settles, because even the best pier report this spring was only rated below average.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (latest 2022-05-18, six days old)**
- Grand Haven pier: "Pier anglers were catching a few coho salmon on alewives or while casting orange spoons." Quality 1 (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18).
- South Haven pier: "Pier fishing remained slow but there was an occasional coho caught on spawn." Quality 1 (South Haven, 2022-05-18).
- St. Joseph pier: "Anglers were also catching an occasional coho. … Nightcrawlers were catching the catfish while spawn was catching the coho." Quality 1 (St. Joseph, 2022-05-18).
- Muskegon: boat reports only. Boats did well, "35 to 90 feet down in 120 to 200 feet of water," on green and blue spoons (Muskegon, 2022-05-18).
- Boats at Grand Haven were rated good, with fish "30 to 120 feet down in 130 to 240 feet of water" (Grand Haven, 2022-05-18). Nothing in the reports says which of these depths applies to the pier.

**Past seasons (history)**
- Searching for weeks with surface water near 52 F turned up only the same 2022-05-18 reports. There are no earlier-season matches to compare, so I have no history to add here.

**Conditions now**
- The conditions tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2022-05-24, not live data. The figures below are from that week.
- Grand Haven pierhead (satellite): avg 51 F, +2 F over the week, +2 F in the last 3 days. Buoy 45029: avg 52 F, −3 F over the week.
- Upwelling wind (north to east, 8+ mph) that week: 26 hours in the last 3 days at Grand Haven, and 30 hours at St. Joseph and South Haven.
- I'd expect a cold push near the piers from that wind. The pier reports for that week were still slow, though, so the upwelling hasn't clearly turned the bite on yet.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are six days old (2022-05-18), and I have no live conditions, only that backtest summary. Check the current weekly report and the local pier before you go.
- The buoy and the satellite pierhead temperatures disagree on direction (buoy down 3 F, satellite up 2 F). The satellite is an approximation off the pier, so don't read too much into it.
- Muskegon has no pier data at all, so its rating is a gap, not a verdict.

## Sources

- DNR bulletin, week of 2022-05-18: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3186585
- DNR bulletin, week of 2022-05-04 (older pier context): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
